info.title: iTop
info.description:
Authentication: static API token (application token or personal token), sent as the Auth-Token header.

iTop is an open-source, web-based IT Service Management and CMDB platform. Its REST/JSON API is a single endpoint (webservices/rest.php) that accepts an `operation` name plus operation-specific parameters (`class`, `key`, `fields`, `output_fields`, ...) and returns a JSON envelope of matching or affected objects. It supports iTop's built-in and custom object classes (tickets such as UserRequest/Incident/Change, CIs, contacts, organizations, and any other class defined in the data model).
info.x-itential-curated: Reviewed against the repo's common-CRUD-for-automation policy: iTop's REST/JSON API is a single operation-dispatch endpoint, and all 1 upstream operations are already in scope, covering list_operations, core/check_credentials, and the core/get, core/create, core/update, core/delete, and core/apply_stimulus actions against any object class (tickets, CIs, contacts, organizations, and custom classes). See the repo README for the operation breakdown and the full spec.

servers.description: Replace ITOP-HOST with your iTop instance's hostname or IP. Set this integration's base_path connection property to the install path plus webservices/rest.php, e.g. /itop/webservices/rest.php.

post.description: Executes an iTop REST/JSON API operation. The specific action (list operations, check credentials, or a core/get, core/create, core/update, core/delete, or core/apply_stimulus CRUD/lifecycle call against any object class) is selected by the `operation` field inside `json_data` — see the request body description and examples.

requestBody.description: REST/JSON operation request, sent as HTML form parameters.

list_operations.summary: List Operations - discover every operation the target iTop supports

check_credentials.summary: Check Credentials - validate a username/password pair

core_get.summary: Core Get - search for objects of a class

value.json_data: {"operation": "core/get", "class": "UserRequest", "key": "SELECT UserRequest WHERE status = 'new'", "output_fields": "id, ref, title, status"}

core_create.summary: Core Create - create a new object

core_update.summary: Core Update - update fields on an existing object

core_delete.summary: Core Delete - delete an existing object

core_apply_stimulus.summary: Core Apply Stimulus - trigger a lifecycle state transition

200.description: Request processed. Check `code` in the response body — iTop always answers with HTTP 200, even for application-level errors.

AuthToken.name: Auth-Token
AuthToken.description: iTop application token or personal token.

json_data.description:
JSON-encoded operation request. Set to a JSON string with an `operation` field plus the parameters that operation requires:

- `list_operations`: `{"operation": "list_operations"}`
- `core/check_credentials`: `{"operation": "core/check_credentials", "user": "...", "password": "..."}`
- `core/get`: `{"operation": "core/get", "class": "UserRequest", "key": "SELECT UserRequest WHERE status = 'new'", "output_fields": "id, ref, title, status"}`
- `core/create`: `{"operation": "core/create", "class": "UserRequest", "fields": {"org_id": "SELECT Organization WHERE name = 'Demo'", "title": "..."}, "output_fields": "id, friendlyname"}`
- `core/update`: `{"operation": "core/update", "class": "UserRequest", "key": 15, "fields": {"status": "assigned"}}`
- `core/delete`: `{"operation": "core/delete", "class": "UserRequest", "key": 15, "simulate": false}`
- `core/apply_stimulus`: `{"operation": "core/apply_stimulus", "class": "UserRequest", "key": 15, "stimulus": "ev_assign", "fields": {"agent_id": 57}}`

`key` accepts a numeric object ID, an OQL query string, or a criteria object. `class` is any object class defined in the target iTop's data model.

code.description: 0 on success; non-zero error codes indicate a failure (bad login, missing object, wrong parameters, security restriction, ...).

objects.description: Map of `Class::key` to the matching/affected object, present for core/get, core/create, core/update, and core/apply_stimulus responses.
